summary: Ernst Kuhn was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Berlin, Leipzig, Tübingen, and Halle-Wittenberg, working under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Heidelberg and Munich.

Ernst Leumann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Zurich, Geneva, Leipzig, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Strasbourg. He held posts at Oxford, Frauenfeld, the University of Strasbourg, and the University of Freiburg.

Ernst Moritz Arndt worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the universities of Greifswald (~1791–1793) and Jena (~1793–1794), and later held posts at Greifswald (~1800–1811) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1860).

Ernst Osiander was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Repetent at Maulbronn, Blaubeuren, and the Tübinger Stift.

Ernst Steinkellner specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. His career includes posts at the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Vienna, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the Tübinger Stift, including under Rudolf von Roth. His career included posts at the East India Company, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Munich.

Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kiel, Göttingen, and Berlin under scholars including Paul Deussen, Emil Sieg, and Heinrich Lüders. He served as professor of Indology at Göttingen (1936–1965).

Ernst Windisch specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Friedrich Zarncke, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs at Leipzig, Heidelberg, and Strasbourg, and worked at the India Office Library.
Ernst Zinn worked in linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (~1941–1945), Saarland University (1951–1956), and the University of Tübingen (~1951–1978).

Erwin Rousselle worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, Darmstadt, and Frankfurt under teachers including Max Walleser. He held posts at Peking University, Yenching University, Tsinghua University, Frankfurt, and the China-Institut Frankfurt.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

Eshin Nishimura specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Hanazono University, Pendle Hill, and Kyoto University, training under Zenkei Shibayama. He served as president and vice-president of Hanazono University and taught at Carleton College.
Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director of Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyujo (attested 1999) and president of the Kyushu Ryukoku Academic Society (attested 2002).
Esho Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University until 2003 and was president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

Esho Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an assistant professorship at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and a professorship at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

Esho Yamaguchi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1944) and later held posts as professor at Osaka University (~1974–1982) and faculty member at Ritsumeikan University (~1982–1989).

Ester Bianchi specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. She completed doctorates at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert. She held posts at the University of Florence and the University of Perugia.
Etienne Vermeersch was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from around 1953 to 1965 and subsequently held an academic post there from 1967 to 1997.

Etsuaki Teraishi works in Indology and philosophy. He held an assistant professorship at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and served as a special researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch was a scholar of Indology, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Vienna under Georg Bühler. He served as Government Epigraphist in India and later held the Sanskrit chair at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).
